beforeRows.summary: The goal-setting surface: the student list with its Action column, the Set Goals / Update Goals / Check Goals control that column shows, and the goal form behind it. What the column offers is decided per student by where they are in the goal cycle.

The goal-setting surface: the student list with its Action column, the Set Goals / Update Goals / Check Goals control that column shows, and the goal form behind it. What the column offers is decided per student by where they are in the goal cycle.
Teacher-facing goal emails go out Mondays, after the Sunday ETL run.

The goal-setting surface: the student list with its Action column, the Set Goals / Update Goals / Check Goals control that column shows, and the goal form behind it. What the column offers is decided per student by where they are in the goal cycle.
Goal-update ETL scripts run Sundays to compute cycle progress and system suggestions. A teacher-set-goal warm-up phase precedes some cycles.

beforeRows.content: Circulates and quietly observes the students.
beforeRows.summary: The teacher moves between breakout rooms without joining any one conversation, keeping a classroom-level view while tutors run goal setting one-on-one. This oversight is what lets the teacher catch a stuck student or tech problem before it derails a pairing.

beforeRows.content: Renames students to match roster names.
beforeRows.summary: The lead tutor corrects a student's display name to match the roster so attendance and pairing stay tied to the right student record, not a Zoom nickname or typo.

The tutor enters the student's individual breakout room in Zoom, which is what starts the one-on-one goal-setting conversation for that pairing. Nothing else in this scenario happens before this join.
The tutor connects with student via Zoom in individual breakout room.

beforeRows.content: Reminds students to keep working while waiting.
beforeRows.summary: While a tutor is still occupied with another student, the teacher keeps waiting students on task rather than idle, so the room does not lose momentum before goal setting starts for them.

beforeRows.content: Adds any un-rostered students to the attendance list.
beforeRows.summary: The lead tutor accounts for a student who joined the session without a matching roster entry, so that student is not dropped from attendance or left unpaired for goal setting. This keeps the session's records accurate even when enrollment data is out of sync.

beforeRows.content: Clicks the 'Update Goals' CTA in the Action column.
beforeRows.summary: The tutor starts the update flow from the dashboard's Action column rather than navigating there manually. The CTA only appears when the app has determined this student is due for a goal update.

The goal-setting surface: the student list with its Action column, the Set Goals / Update Goals / Check Goals control that column shows, and the goal form behind it. What the column offers is decided per student by where they are in the goal cycle.
Dev Team builds the app and the Design Team creates the screens and flows relevant to this step. Both implement the findings from the research team into the app in their respective role.

beforeRows.content: Checks if all students are in the correct breakout room.
beforeRows.summary: Before the tutor pairs settle in, the teacher confirms every student landed in their assigned breakout room rather than a wrong or empty one. This catch happens before goal setting starts, since a misrouted student has no tutor to set goals with.

beforeRows.content: Manually assigns unpaired students to available tutors.
beforeRows.summary: When automatic pairing leaves a student without a tutor, the lead tutor steps in to assign one by hand so goal setting is not skipped for that student. This is the fallback for whatever caused the pairing to fail in the first place.

The tutor shares their screen so the student can see the same goal-setting view the tutor is working from, rather than describing it verbally. This is what lets the tutor walk the student through the exact fields being filled in.
The tutor shares screen via Zoom screen share feature.
Dev Team builds the app and the Design Team creates the screens and flows relevant to this step. Both implement the findings from the research team into the app in their respective role.

beforeRows.content: Receives information that a student is absent from the session.
beforeRows.summary: The teacher is the one told when a student does not show, which is what triggers roster and pairing adjustments for the rest of the session. This is the first step in reconciling attendance against the goal-setting plan for that class.

beforeRows.content: Inform classroom teacher about students that are absent.
Reviews the last goal cycle overview and system suggestion.
beforeRows.summary: Before updating anything, the tutor and student look at how the previous cycle went and the app's suggested next goal, so the new goal is informed by actual progress rather than set cold. The suggestion is generated by the app, not chosen by the tutor.
The tutor connects with student via Zoom in individual breakout room.

beforeRows.content: PLUS App provides goal support for every school.
beforeRows.summary: Goal setting is mandatory for every school since October 2026. The dashboard Action column routes the student to Set goals, Update goals or Check goals according to their goal-cycle state.

beforeRows.content: Alerts lead tutor about unassigned or miss-assigned students using the "ask for help" alert.
Respond to classroom teachers "ask for help" request.
Starts updating the goal for the new goal cycle while sharing screen once the student understands.

beforeRows.content: Handles student tech problems as they arise.
beforeRows.summary: The teacher is the first responder for device or connection issues during the breakout, so a tutor can stay focused on the goal-setting conversation instead of troubleshooting. Without this, a tech problem would either interrupt the tutor or go unresolved.

beforeRows.content: Explains each suggested value, asks if it feels right, and enters the student's choice for the effort and progress goals.
beforeRows.summary: System recommendations are starting points. The tutor explains each suggested goal and gives the student time to respond, then records the student's preference within the app's limits.
The tutor connects with student via Zoom in individual breakout room.
